description.summary: desktop shell control of compositor state

protocol.description: Compositor features a desktop shell configures that no standard protocol covers. Only unsandboxed clients see these globals. Outputs are named by their connector, as in zwlr_output_head_v1.name.

interface.name: dsk_output_manager_v1
interface.description: Mirroring an output removes it from the desktop and shows another output's frames on it, scaled to fit. Mode, scale, position, and enablement stay on zwlr_output_manager_v1. The compositor persists mirror changes.

request.name: set_mirror
request.description: The result arrives as a mirror or failed event for target.

event.name: mirror
event.description: Sent for every connected output on bind, and for an output whenever its mirror state changes. An empty source means not mirroring.

description.summary: end of the initial state batch

event.name: failed
event.description: Unknown output, a source that is itself a mirror, or target equal to source.

interface.name: dsk_input_manager_v1
interface.description: Input settings named by their config keys ("input.touchpad.tap"), with values as plain text ("true", "0.3", "adaptive", "us,de"). An empty value means unset, which restores the device or built-in default. The compositor validates, applies, and persists every change.

request.name: set
request.description: Answered by setting events and done, or by failed.

event.name: device_added
event.description: Sent for every connected device on bind and whenever one connects.

event.name: setting
event.description: Sent for every setting on bind and after every configuration change. locked is 1 when the user's own config file sets the key, which wins over changes made here.

description.summary: end of a batch of events

interface.name: dsk_shell_v1
interface.description: Bound by the desktop shell. Keybinds that drive the shell arrive as action events on the connection the shell already holds, so no process is started per keypress. The compositor also reports the keyboard lock-key state it owns, so the shell never polls LEDs.

event.name: action
event.description: A command line in the shell's own command language, as typed after the shell's IPC verb, for example "panel-toggle launcher".

event.name: lock_keys
event.description: Sent on bind and whenever the state changes. Each argument is 1 when that lock is active and 0 otherwise.
